1: Maya met three th- words on Monday: through, think and there. All three slowed her down. On each one she tried the pieces before anything else, and that is the move we want. For think and there, the page said th and she read the rest herself. For through, the page said the whole word once and she read it back. Nothing has clicked yet, and that is fine for a first page. She needed a break after 6 minutes on Monday. The next page is shorter, and the same three words come back next to words she already owns. If she stalls on a word at homework time, cover everything but the first piece with your finger and wait.
3: Two of the th- words clicked so far this week: think and there. She read both without help on Tuesday and again on Wednesday. Through is still slowing her. On Tuesday and Wednesday she only needed the pieces, th and rough, and then read it herself. That is less help than Monday, when the page had to say the whole word once. For now through comes back twice on every page, sitting next to words she already owns. She needed a break after 6 minutes on Monday and 9 minutes on Wednesday. At homework time, read one short page with her and then stop, even when it is going well. Tuesday was a short page, and Wednesday was her longest sit yet.
7: Four words clicked this week: through, think, there and which. Through took until Thursday, and since then she has read it on every page without help. Which slowed her once, on Thursday, and not since. Where is still slowing her. She needed the pieces on Thursday, Friday and Saturday. On Sunday she read it by herself for the first time. It comes back twice on every page for now, next to words she already owns. She needed a break after 6 minutes on Monday, 9 minutes on Wednesday and 11 minutes on Friday. At homework time, let her pick the book or the page, the way she picks what Biscuit does next on the break card.
